text:
$NVDA today announces capacity agreements with substrate, packaging, testing and optical engine suppliers.

- Substrate agreements with Ibiden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron to expand by 2.5x
- $AMKR to increase advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028, with a new $1.3B agreement
- Multibillion dollar capacity reservation advance to support Ibiden's plant in Japan
- "By 2028, production allocated to $NVDA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics' total annual package substrate production capacity"
- KYEC with $1.1B capacity reservation in advance
- SPIL for optical engine capacity for CPO by 15x by H2 2027 and double that for 2028

Well, that's a lot of news. As Jensen Huang puts it: "Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint."

name: Charlie Bilello
zh_summary: @charliebilello details $META Q3 revenues up 26% YoY to a record $64.6 billion, but costs/expenses rose 68% YoY to $51.6 billion including $9.9 billion from a $18.6 billion teen mental health settlement, causing operating income to fall 37% YoY to $13 billion and margins to drop to 20% from 40%.
en_summary: @charliebilello details $META Q3 revenues up 26% YoY to a record $64.6 billion, but costs/expenses rose 68% YoY to $51.6 billion including $9.9 billion from a $18.6 billion teen mental health settlement, causing operating income to fall 37% YoY to $13 billion and margins to drop to 20% from 40%.
text: Meta Q3 revenues increased 26% over the last year to a new record high of $64.6 billion. But costs/expenses rose 68% YoY to a record $51.6 billion ($9.9 billion of this was part of the $18.6 billion settlement related to teen mental health/social media).
